To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new approach to isocenter quality assessment using portal images is described and demonstrated.

a quality assurance approach for linear accelerator mechanical isocenters with portal images was described and demonstrated to provide an alternative with superior accuracy, robustness and reproducibility.
an EPID-based iscenter QA approach is described, demonstrated to be accurate and robust, and provides a superior alternative for isocenter QA with no additional cost.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an EPID-based QA approach to verify the isocenter quality of a linear accelerator.
the design and development of an innovative isocenter QA system for linear accelerators.
a new isocenter QA method for linear accelerators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this EPID-based isometric QA is a superior alternative to current QA methods.
the proposed EPID-based approach is a superior alternative for isocenter QA of the linear accelerator.
the proposed approach is a superior alternative to the conventional isocenter test and should become the standard of care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach is a valuable addition to the QA toolbox of the radiation therapy community.
the EPID-based isochenter QA is a superior alternative to the current conventional QA methods for isochenter verification.
this EPID-based isometric QA approach can serve as an excellent tool for routine isocenter QA, especially for SRS/SBRT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
portal imaging is an effective and accurate tool for isocenter QA.
EPID-based QA can be applied to any rotating system in a Linac.
EPID images can be used to determine isocenter location with high precision and accuracy.
